title: I released my AI-assisted game demo for Steam Next Fest. How can I grow visibility and wishlists from a small base?
author: Fearless-Pin-7761
selftext:
Hi everyone! I've released the free Windows demo of CATadel: Slot Defense on Steam, and it's participating in Steam Next Fest. You spin slots to build a cat army, earn gold through battles, and decide how much to spend on upgrades versus save for the royal tax bill.

I've spent over three months building and refining it. My background is in 3D animation, mainly Blender and Unreal Engine. When continuing that work became difficult, AI tools made it possible for me to try developing a game I'd previously only imagined making.

I used generative AI extensively throughout production, including for the vast majority of the game's assets and models. The game design is mine. **Most models started from AI-generated results**, and I corrected awkward models and UVs in Blender myself. I also reviewed the implementation and animations individually. There is no real-time AI generation during gameplay.

The demo has had more than ten updates since release. One recurring piece of feedback has been that the beginning is hard to understand, so I'd especially appreciate a fresh player's perspective.

From this 20-second clip, is the basic idea of the game clear? What catches your attention, and what feels confusing? Does it make you curious enough to try the demo?

If you do try the demo, I'd also appreciate honest feedback on the gameplay, especially the introduction, the choices, and anything that becomes repetitive.

My wishlist count has nearly doubled during Steam Next Fest, but it's still under 500. Alongside gameplay feedback, I'd also welcome advice on reaching players who might enjoy this kind of game. If you've released an AI-assisted game, what helped you find the right audience?

Free Windows demo: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5273060/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5273060/)

Thanks for taking a look and sharing your thoughts!
